name: Historical Case Transfer Gate

positioning.oneLineSummary: Blocks a famous success or failure from becoming a scoring rule until decision-time comparability, base rates, mechanisms, and counterexamples are established.
positioning.productLabel: Historical Case Transfer Guardrail — derived from The Power Law's public historical method
notAClaimOf: a named investor endorsing the product

attribution.display: Product guardrail informed by Sebastian Mallaby's public historical analysis

neutralParaphrase: Use historical venture cases to surface mechanisms, hypotheses, and counterexamples. Before applying a lesson to a current deal, compare stage, era, technology, capital intensity, market structure, terms, and information available at the time, and expose missing base rates and survivorship.

locator.value: Official description of successes, disasters, firm strategies, and industry shortcomings
Transcript discussion of elite-case focus, data opacity, skill, luck, and reputation feedback
Abstract on noisy VC performance and difficulty identifying skill

requiredConditions: A historical case is invoked in a current analysis.
Decision-time rather than outcome-only evidence can be reconstructed.
The case contributes no formal weight by default.

requiredEvidence.description: Sources for what happened, what was knowable then, decisions, context, and outcome.
Stage, era, technology, market, capital, security, geography, and causal-mechanism comparison.
Failures or alternate cases sharing the same visible traits.

decisionQuestions: What mechanism, not surface resemblance, makes the case relevant?
What information was available before the outcome?
What countercases share the same visible features?
Does the case generate a question or improperly dictate a conclusion?
positiveSignals: The causal mechanism is comparable and independently evidenced.
Decision-time information and countercases are represented.
The case produces a falsifiable evidence request.
Outcome prestige does not alter formal weight.
redFlags: The report says this is the next famous winner.
Only winners or scandals are retrieved.
Present knowledge is projected into the historical decision.
A tactic is copied without its firm system and era.
disconfirmingEvidence: The current company differs on the relevant causal mechanism.
The historical result depended on a unique regulatory or capital environment.
Countercases are more numerous or more comparable.
The claimed lesson appears only after the outcome.
contraindications: Do not allow historical analogy to carry formal decision weight.
Do not imply endorsement by named investors or firms.
Do not use a case when only a secondary summary is available.

instructions: Identify the precise claim the case is being used to support.
Retrieve countercases and missing base rates.
Conclude transferable hypothesis, weak analogy, non-transferable, or insufficient source.

sourceReliability.medium: Well-sourced history and some primary record.
sourceReliability.high: Contemporaneous primary records plus independent history and countercases.

evidenceStrength.high: Mechanism is comparable, causal, current, and counter-tested.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Context and mechanism covered; base rate partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Decision-time evidence, context, mechanism, outcome, countercases, and base-rate limitations complete.

applicabilityConfidence.low: No case is used or context differs materially.
applicabilityConfidence.high: A precise historical claim materially informs current research.

judgmentConfidence.medium: Case supports a research hypothesis only.
judgmentConfidence.high: Case supplies a bounded transferable mechanism, still with zero formal weight.

promotionRequirements: Validate case provenance and countercase retrieval.
empiricalQualifications: Elite histories are selected and narratively coherent after the fact.

rights.notes: Historical material is used only as neutral, source-linked research context.

openIssues: Make this gate mandatory before runtime case analogies are displayed.
